correctness.rationale: For independent fair nearest-neighbor lattice walkers started at 2 and stopped when any reaches 0, reflection gives Pr(tau_1>2m)=Pr(tau_1>2m+1)=a_m=(2m+1)/(m+1)*C(2m,m)/4^m. Thus mu_N=2 sum_m a_m^N, h_N=sum_m(4m+1)a_m^N and mu finite iff N>2, h finite iff N>4. Geometric reset after failed steps gives exact mean (1-q)(1-f_N(q))/(q f_N(q)), f_N=E(1-q)^tau, yielding right derivative mu²-mu-h for N>=5 and -infinity N3,4. Source check_restart.py provides outward integer fixed-point sums through m=9999 with analytical Wallis/integral remainder bounds, giving h+mu-mu² positive N5,6 (D6 in (0.082,0.084)), negative N7,8 and h9<2; monotonicity hN<=h9 and muN>=2 completes N>=9. Fresh independent long-series numerical sums corroborated approximate D5=3.8973,D6=0.08287,D7=-0.67706,D8=-0.90187, but unrestricted sign rests on the rigorous tail certificate, not truncation. N1,2 unreset infinite while any positive q has finite mean.
